PraisonAIUI can host any AI agent backend behind a modular dashboard shell: pages, views, layout components, optional plugins, and branding — without forking the frontend.

Extension priority (first match wins): window.aiui.registerView(pageId, …) Dashboard manifest plugins (dashboard-plugins/*/manifest.json) Built-in view modules: views/ .js for built-in pages, from /api/shell/manifest (a page's source and kind there decide; an app page under a built-in id renders its own content, also in the dashboard style) Server aiui.layout() JSON from @aiui.page() window.aiui.registerComponent(type, …) inside renderComponent Generic JSON fallback viewer

Define pages with @aiui.page() returning aiui.layout([...]). Types are implemented once in ui.py and dashboard.js. Kanban / board: use aiui.board(columns=[...]). Columns contain id, title, and cards (from aiui.card() or dicts). The shell renders via renderBoard, composing existing card renderers (DRY).

Load heavy built-ins only when listed: This adds jobs.js, auth.js, or api.js to the plugin chain; their pages resolve to views/ .js for built-in pages, from /api/shell/manifest. feedback is always available as a built-in view when the page is enabled.

Add new layout types in ui.py and one case in dashboard.js. Page-specific UI belongs in plugins/views/*.js, delegating to shared modules (jobs.js, etc.) via thin wrappers. Reuse _helpers.js (pageToolbar, filterChips, searchInput, modalShell, toast). Boards compose card / columns — do not duplicate card markup in plugins.
